summary: A 1935 CCC-built ground house on Sugarloaf Mountain in Chiricahua National Monument; the register says unstaffed and sources disagree on build details, but a public trail reaches it.

facts.design: 14x14 ft ground house with stone base and permanent overhang roof per NHLR; the CCC narrative describes frame construction on a masonry foundation with concrete basement, cistern and hardwood floors

access.note: Reached by a public hiking trail in Chiricahua National Monument. The sources do not say whether visitors may enter the cabin, and NPS still uses it to monitor summer lightning.

visit.trail_note: Sugarloaf Mountain Trail: moderate, 1.8 miles (2.8 km) round trip, starts at the Sugarloaf parking lot, uphill with little rough terrain.

events.note: Built by CCC enrollees from Camp NM-2-A as a fire lookout house; Company 828 began excavation and materials were packed in by mule; the narrative says it was finished in summer and fall 1935

Wikidata gives a 21 November 2008 start time for a National Register contributing-property claim within the Chiricahua National Monument Historic Designed Landscape; the NPS page confirms the landscape is on the Register but I did not confirm this date

notes_for_editor: Brief's record (1935 built, NHLR 2004 registration, NPS agency, unknown access) checks out. Access can move from unknown to public for the hiking trail, but whether visitors may enter the cabin is not documented. Sources disagree on build details (stone base in the register vs frame on masonry in the narrative) and the narrative also has a 'by 1937' summary that is compatible with the 1935 finish but less precise. Summit elevation (NPS 7,310 ft) differs from the register's lookout elevation (7,238 ft). No specific fire at the lookout was found. The 2008 NRHP date is Wikidata-only. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows coordinates 32.01414, -109.32508, slightly off the register's 32.01111, -109.32639.
